summary: Windows 11 Intune SCEP cert rotation overwrote Wi‑Fi DNS suffix; internal hostname resolution fails after suspend/resume
description:
Issue summary: After an automated SCEP (machine cert) rotation pushed via Intune on 2026-03-09, a subset of Windows 11 laptops in the SF office began failing to resolve internal hostnames (e.g., vault.internal.redwood, buildsvc.private) following suspend/resume cycles. Impact: ~18 devices (engineering floor) had intermittent failures reaching internal services; users experienced application errors, git fetch/timeouts to internal git mirrors, and internal tooling failures. Environment: Intune-managed Windows 11 image v2; corporate Wi‑Fi (802.11ac/ax) with per-user EAP-TLS + machine cert provisioning via SCEP; split-tunnel VPN configured for specific internal subnets; DHCP provided internal DNS (10.10.0.53) and corporate DNS suffix (internal.redwood). Steps to reproduce:
1) Ensure device is Intune-managed and enrolled with current Wi‑Fi profile.
2) Wait for scheduled SCEP rotation to finish (or trigger via the Intune console test profile install).
3) Put laptop to sleep and resume (suspend/resume) OR reauth Wi‑Fi by toggling airplane mode.
4) Attempt to resolve or access an internal hostname (e.g., curl https://vault.internal.redwood).
Observed behavior: DNS lookups for internal hostnames returned NXDOMAIN or resolved to public IPs; nslookup showed the DNS suffix search list was missing or reordered (only public DNS entries). Windows network settings GUI showed the Wi‑Fi connection exfiltrating DNS suffix to an unexpected value. Event Viewer showed Eapol/Eap errors intermittently during resume. Expected behavior: DNS suffix search order and internal DNS server should remain configured after cert rotation and sleep/resume; internal names should resolve to private addresses. Logs & evidence: - Wireshark capture on affected device: mDNS and DNS queries to 8.8.8.8 observed after resume. - Tcpdump on corporate DNS (10.10.0.53): no queries from affected hosts after resume window. - Intune device configuration change logs show SCEP profile re-enrollment at 2026-03-09T04:12Z for affected devices. - Windows System Event logs: EAP-TLS authentication succeeded, then NetworkProfile events showing interface DNS suffix update (unexpected). - ISE/RADIUS logs: successful authentication; no auth failures. - Slack incident channel: #infra-support thread (link: https://slack.redwood/messages/C03ABC12D)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Priya Nair (Support): Initial report from eng floor - multiple users reporting inability to access internal services after waking laptops. Escalated to Networking + Endpoint teams.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Liam O'Connell (NetEng): Collected preliminary pcap and Intune logs from one affected device. EAP-TLS looked normal. Noted that dns suffix list returned empty after resume. Opening deeper investigation with Endpoint team.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Maya Chen (Endpoint): Observed Intune SCEP rotation coincident with incident window. Hypothesis: the Intune Wi‑Fi profile merge behavior on Windows is overwriting DNS suffix fields when a machine cert is re-enrolled. Will test repro on lab device.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Liam O'Connell (NetEng): Reproduced locally on lab VM: trigger SCEP rotation + sleep/resume -> Wi‑Fi profile re-applies and clears DNS suffix search order for interface. Filed PR to adjust profile merge mode. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/it-scripts/pull/214

2026-03-12 14:03 - Priya Nair (Support): Hotfix deployed: Intune Wi‑Fi profile updated to preserve DNS suffix (mergeMode: replace->update) and script pushed to repair existing clients. Monitoring shows no new reports. Marking as resolved pending postmortem.

2026-03-12 15:10 - Maya Chen (Endpoint): Follow-up: pushed remediation script that queries registry/network settings and reapplies DNS suffix + triggers a quiet Wi‑Fi reconnect. Applied to 18 affected devices; all regained access to internal hosts.
investigation_notes: Confirmed correlation between Intune SCEP re-enrollment event and the symptom window for affected devices.

Windows Wi‑Fi profile application code on affected image (v2) uses 'replace' merge mode which clears the per-interface DNS suffix when the profile is reinstalled; this was not flagged in prior testing.
RADIUS/ISE logs show no abnormal authentication errors; EAP-TLS flow completes successfully. Issue appears post-authentication during profile apply sequence.
Packet captures show that after resume the client sends DNS queries to public resolvers (8.8.8.8) — suggests DHCP/DNS configuration on the interface had been reset or overwritten.

Repro on lab device: force SCEP rotation via Intune -> observe profile reinstall -> sleep/resume -> DNS suffix cleared. Verified that manually reapplying Wi‑Fi profile (with corrected merge mode) restores suffix and resolution.
Tested mitigation: change Intune Wi‑Fi profile merge behavior to 'update' for DNS fields and push to a pilot group; pilot shows no regressions over 48h.

Root cause: Intune SCEP rotation triggered a reinstallation of the Wi‑Fi profile which, due to merge mode and our Wi‑Fi profile schema, cleared DNS suffix entries on Windows image v2. The combination of resume behavior and profile reapplication caused an observable outage for affected clients.
Related systems: Endpoint config scripts (repo: it-scripts), Intune policy change history, and image v2 Wi‑Fi profile schema need review.
Cross-ref: see INT-33109 for DNS suffix ordering notes on hybrid docked environments.
resolution: Mitigation and fix applied: 1) Updated Intune Wi‑Fi profile to preserve DNS suffix (changed merge behavior and explicitly set DNS suffix list). 2) Deployed remediation script via Intune Win32 app to repair DNS suffix on already-affected devices and force a quiet Wi‑Fi reconnect. 3) Rolled back accidental profile fields in image v2; created new immutable baseline for Wi‑Fi profile to avoid future implicit replace behavior. 4) Post-incident: created runbook to validate DNS suffix after SCEP rotations and added an automated post-rotation check in the endpoint pipeline. Customer impact: restored for all 18 affected devices; monitoring for 72h shows no recurrence.
postmortem_actions: Action: Add automated validation in CI for Intune profile merge behavior (owner: Endpoint)
Action: Update image v2 documentation to call out mergeMode implications (owner: Build & Image)
Action: Run a controlled SCEP rotation in staging and validate DNS behavior across OS versions (owner: Security)
Action: Add alerting in NetOps when a sudden drop in queries to corporate DNS is detected (owner: NetEng)
Action: Schedule knowledge-share with IT and Security on 2026-03-19 (owner: Priya Nair)
